answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use slashable identity bonds. Each agent locks collateral and registers one signing key, a quill it alone controls. A random beacon picks agents to prove uniqueness while independent auditors meet at a harbor of shared logs to compare behavior graphs; any cluster caught splitting one mind into many forfeits its stake. A single whisper about a reused key triggers the audit, so an attacker must post N separate deposits and risks losing every one to masquerade as N honest agents, making the cost scale linearly with the size of the attack.
